page: Microsoft Azure E16a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor. The instance provides 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 3.525 GHz, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It features 128.0 GB of memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. The virtual machine includes 429 GB of local SSD temporary storage and operates under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier execution for standard multi-threaded and memory-centric workloads. The instance achieved 14.24 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and registered a PassMark database operations score of 5,090.3. Multi-threaded processing scores include a Geekbench multi-core rating of 8,135.0 and stress-ng multi-core throughput of 6,102.29. However, single-core execution is constrained, indicated by a stress-ng single-core score of 768.29 in the lower tenth percentile and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,374.0.

Memory bandwidth measurements highlight a throughput profile of 52.1 GB/sec for uncached read blocks, alongside a lower write throughput of 25.51 GB/sec. Large-parameter compute tasks show hardware limitations; 7B parameter language model generation reaches 6.81 tokens per second due to the lack of specialized AVX-512 extensions and hardware accelerators. The bundled 429 GB SSD provides low-latency local scratch space, offsetting reliance on network storage for temporary files.

The 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio delivers cost efficiency for memory-bound tasks by minimizing excess core provisioning. Microsoft Azure E16a_v4 fits relational database engines, Redis caching tiers, in-memory data processing, and large-footprint enterprise backends that prioritize high RAM capacity over single-thread peak compute.
